model: Tecogen InVerde Ultra 100 CHP via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Tecogen InVerde Ultra 100 inverter-based CHP modules on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Tecogen InVerde Ultra 100: 277 objects (158 AI, 93 BI, 26 BO), but only 20 polled by default: the ready/startup/run/shutdown LEDs plus battery voltage, rpm, voltages, currents, power per leg and frequency. The rest of the map (engine and inverter analog values, alarm bits, relay outputs and start/stop/reset flags) is in the profile unpolled.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile TECOGEN_INV_100_a_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the InVerde 100 Modbus register list (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/TecogenINV-100.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 20 of the 277 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (Counter 1; Counter 2; Counter 3...); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Read the Run and Ready LEDs, average power and voltage. Start/stop and alarm reset flags (BO 24-26) exist but are unpolled; check the Tecogen register document before writing them.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: LED and relay states are Binary Outputs (coils) in this profile; reading them is safe, writing them is not.
Several values are scaled by 10 as the names say.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
